key_findings.most_improved_element: Slug optimization (+35 points average) through strategic shortening and keyword reordering
optimization_techniques_that_worked: Question format in titles and descriptions (used in 8/10 articles)
Specific countable values (3 tests, 4 signs, 5 warnings, 6 symptoms, 12 foods)
Shortened slugs using abbreviations (bp for blood-pressure, 50s for 50-59)
Urgency words (today, essential, must-know, warning, urgent)
'Your' instead of 'The' for emotional ownership (used in 6/10 titles)
First-person questions ('Why Do I...?') for strong identification
Concrete action verbs (Stop, Get, Discover, Keep) vs passive (Learn, Understand)
Opening with audience identification in descriptions
Specific problems over vague benefits (stop reflux vs improve digestion)
Strategic keyword reordering in slugs for SEO (low-blood-sugar first)

recommendations.standards_validation: YES - The new standards are highly effective. All 10 articles achieved 85+ scores (average 93), compared to only 0/10 previously. The standards provide clear, actionable criteria that consistently produce compelling, SEO-optimized metadata.
recommendations.next_steps: STRONGLY RECOMMEND proceeding with large-scale optimization of 2209 articles using these standards. The consistent improvement (+19 points average overall) demonstrates the standards are reliable and repeatable.
potential_adjustments: Consider adding 'voice test' - if you wouldn't say it to a friend, rewrite it
Create template library for common article types (X foods, warning signs, guide for caregivers)
Develop quick-reference cheat sheet of high-performing opening phrases
Add A/B testing framework for titles with similar scores (90+ range)
Consider industry-specific abbreviations checklist (bp, ckd, hrt, ssri all tested well)
